answer: Practically, the chain should bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because falcon only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, terrace is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
